findings: 54 columns ending in _id lack FK constraints — audited each for orphaned/invalid references

False positives: amount_paid (4 tables), is_paid (2), payrolls.payroll_id (display code PAY-YYYY-NNNN), uuid, telegram_chat_id, credential_id, device_id, terminal_id, biometric_id, provider_message_id — these are not foreign keys at all

Polymorphic pairs verified via *_type columns: notifications.related_id, payment_receipts/references.payable_id, payment_settlements.settleable_id, visit_invoices.invoiceable_id, inventory_logs/activity_logs.reference_id, email_deliveries.source_id — all resolve to existing parent rows
Correctly-typed plain references (service_request_id, user_id, customer_id, pet_id, service_id): 0 orphans
CONCLUSION: no orphaned or invalid references found; absence of FK constraints is a design characteristic (no cascade protection), not a data-integrity violation
Local audit DB is MariaDB 10.4 — NOT MySQL 8; local results are not proof of MySQL 8 behavior
sql_mode lacks ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY and STRICT_TRANS_TABLES — queries with non-aggregated selected columns absent from GROUP BY pass locally but FAIL on MySQL 8 defaults
73 groupBy call sites across controllers (Reports, Inventory, Dashboard, CustomerReport, Chatbot, ActivityLog, LoginLog, ReconcileEmailDeliveries) are the primary OFGB risk surface
Two migrations contain CHECK constraints — MariaDB 10.2+ enforces them, MySQL >=8.0.16 enforces them, older MySQL ignores — consistent behavior on MySQL 8
CI (per .github/workflows/ci.yml + AGENTS.md) runs the full backend suite on MySQL 8 — that pipeline is the authoritative parity gate for tested paths
RECOMMENDATION: treat CI MySQL 8 suite as the parity gate; audit the 73 groupBy sites for ONLY_FULL_GROUP_BY safety before claiming full parity
